title: Crash on M1 mac,Intel Linux using vulkan mobile renderer
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible on Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - 
    - Vulkan (Mobile) - **integrated Apple M1 - Apple M1** (8 threads)
- Reproducible on Godot v4.4.1.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor
    - Vulkan (Mobile) - **integrated Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2)** - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H (14 threads)
- Not reproducible on Godot v4.4.1.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor
    - Vulkan (Mobile) - **dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU** - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H (14 threads)
    - Vulkan 1.3.255 - Forward+ Intel - Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2)
    - OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 23.2.1-1ubuntu3.1~22.04.3 - Intel(R) Graphics (ADL GT2)
- Not reproducible on Godot v4.4.1.stable -  macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor
    - Metal 3.2 - Forward Mobile -  Apple M1 (Apple7)
    - OpenGL API 4.1 Metal - 89.4 - Compatibility
    - Vulkan (Forward+) produced a warning: `[mvk-error] VK_INCOMPLETE: Error writing pipeline cache data: Failed to write 4 bytes to output stream! Wrote 0`

### System information

### Steps to reproduce

Many omnilight shadows with CubeMap projection in Vulkan mobile rendering mode, on M1(mac) or Intel(linux) gpu.

The reproduction required at least 29 omnilights with shadows per viewport, and multiple active viewports.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This project reproduces the issue on Intel/Linux and macos M1:

[omni-shadow-mobile2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20541616/omni-shadow-mobile2.zip)
